split.3a: v2 (L32): TRAIN/VAL = GLC landslides in ~50 km blocks, S+SE Brazil, no RS 2024 points; TEST = held-out Brazilian event slides vs random land
split.3b: TRAIN/VAL = dated GLC/COOLR landslides worldwide, split by event; TEST = held-out events (see test_events), never seen in training; GFS scored only on issue days with an archived run

t_ml_ranking_note: 3a TEST PR-AUC, calibrated (served scores): best = xgb_terrain_only 0.765; xgb_all 0.747; rf_all 0.706; xgb_terrain_landcover 0.696. Raw (pre-calibration) scores: best = xgb_terrain_only 0.765; xgb_all 0.747; rf_all 0.706; xgb_terrain_landcover 0.696. Isotonic calibration (VAL-fit step function) creates ties that lower ranking metrics.

served.note: Live layer = xgb_rain_soil (daily model, P_H = 1 - prod(1 - p_day)). On VAL direct_rain (one model per horizon) ranks slightly higher; the live service runs one daily model, so xgb_rain_soil stays served and both are reported on TEST.

val_vs_test_note: VAL = held-out GLC/COOLR events (worldwide, mostly 2015-2018, perfect forecast); TEST = held-out disaster events. VAL PR-AUC (24h ~0.13) is ~5x lower than TEST (~0.62): base rates differ and TEST events are large, well-defined storms. An independent overfit audit is checking whether TEST is easier by design; read TEST next to VAL.
